subject: general
question: Comptroller and Auditor General of India submits the audit reports to ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Article 151 - Audit reports

__
 
• CAG submits audit reports relating the accounts of the Centre to the **president**, who shall, in turn, place them before both Houses of Parliament, similar
 
• CAG submits audit reports relating the accounts of the state to the governor, who shall, in turn, place them before the state legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Constitution of India ( Article 148 ) Provides an independent office of the Comptroller and Audit General of India ( CAG ). He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
 
• Article 148 - Comptroller and Auditor General of India
 
• He holds office for a period of six years or up to the age of 65 years (whichever is earlier).
 
• Appointed by – The President
 
• Salaries/allowance - Second Schedule
 
• Removal – similar to Supreme Court Judge
 
• Further office - Not Eligible after Retirement
 
• Administrative Expenses – Charged upon Consolidated Fund of India
 
• Article 149 – Authorises the Parliament to prescribe the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General in relation to the accounts of the Union and the states and any other authority or body.
 
• Article 150 - Form of accounts of the Union and the states.
 
• CAG advises the President about prescriptions in which the accounts of the Centre and the states shall be kept.
